Angles written ∠ are read from the figure. Let M be the midpoint of BC. Let N be the midpoint of AC.

Plan: it suffices to show that △AHG ∼ △MOG.

1. G is the centroid of △ABC, so AG : GM = 2. (1)

2. OA = OC and NA = NC, so ON is the perpendicular bisector of AC; hence ON ⟂ AC. (2)

3. OB = OC and MB = MC, so OM is the perpendicular bisector of BC; hence OM ⟂ BC. (3)

4. AH ⟂ BC and OM ⟂ BC, by (3), so AH ∥ OM. (4)

5. We show that △AHB ∼ △MON:

∠BAH = 90° − ∠B    [AH ⟂ BC]
     = 90° − ∠NMC    [MN is a midline of △CBA]
     = ∠NMO    [OM ⟂ BC, by (3)]

∠HBA = 90° − ∠A    [BH ⟂ AC]
     = 90° − ∠CNM    [MN is a midline of △CBA]
     = ∠ONM    [ON ⟂ AC, by (2)]

Hence △AHB ∼ △MON (AA). (5)

6. AH ∥ OM, by (4), so ∠GAH = ∠AMO.

MG / AG = 1 / 2    [AG : GM = 2, by (1)]
        = MN / AB    [MN is a midline of △CBA]
        = OM / AH    [△AHB ∼ △MON, by (5)]

Hence △AHG ∼ △MOG (SAS). (6)

7. △AHG ∼ △MOG, by (6), so ∠AGH = ∠MGO; as A, G, M are collinear and these two angles lie on opposite sides of that line, they are vertical angles, so O, G, H are collinear, as required. ∎
